page.layout: One page of text in a single column, with the running head at top and the page number at top right. Below the text: a decorative woodcut strip, then the chapter heading "CAPVT X." with its subtitle, then a block of italic lines beside a small woodcut ornament at left. Signature "d.ij." at the foot right. No marginal notes.

main_text.p: ignotas ; hominibus manifeftasse. Cuius filius dicatur [?]בר קובא Barkubba, id est, filius prostitutæ & meretricis, vt ait Epiphanius. Ita illi in meras nugas sacram Scripturam transformant, dum [?]ἰδίαν ἐπίλυσιν in Prophetarum & Verbi diuini interpretatione sequuntur & afferunt. Simile quiddam habent Saturniniani. 3 Error.
Plura Euangelia, & alia habent quàm vera. Habent enim Euangelium perfectionis quod vocant, carmine scriptum, & Euangelium Euæ.

4 Visiones, [?]ἐνθουσιασμὸς, priuatas reuelationes atque falsa miracula iactant, quemadmodum olim Mirabiliarij, & nunc Anabaptistæ, vt sua deliria confirment. Ab his enim Anabaptistarum [?]ἐνθουσιασμοὶ videntur petiti. 5 Esse eiusdem substantiæ animam quæ in hominibus, brutis animantibus, & plantis ipsis insit, quem errorem postea Manichæi sunt amplexi. Ita error latius propagatus est.
main_text.head: CAPVT X. Ebionitorum error duplex. Ebionitis autem accensentur Sampsei, & Elcefei vel Elcefaitæ: & quid hi postremi ab Ebionitis differant.
main_text.p: Bionei{1} Christum etiam tantummodò {2}hominem dicunt. Mandata carnalia Legis obseruant, Circuncisionem scilicet carnis, & catera, à quorum oneribus per Nouum Testamentum liberati sumus. Huic hæresi Epiphanius Sampseos, & Elcesios ita copulat, vt sub

page.notes: Reference marks {1} and {2} after "Bionei" and before "hominem" stand in the italic block; no matching notes are printed on this page. Doubtful readings: the Hebrew word "בר קובא" (Barkubba) and the Greek words ἰδίαν ἐπίλυσιν, ἐνθουσιασμὸς and ἐνθουσιασμοὶ are marked [?]. The "3" and "4" and "5" numbers within paragraphs are kept inline as printed. The decorative block beside the italic lines is an ornament, not text.
